## **Indian Army Structure**

The Indian Army is headed by the **Chief of Army Staff (COAS)**, currently a 4-star General.

### **Basic Structure**

* **Army Headquarters (New Delhi)**  
* **Commands**  
* **Corps**  
* **Divisions**  
* **Brigades**  
* **Battalions**  
* **Companies**  
* **Platoons**  
* **Sections**

### **Major Fighting Arms**

* Infantry  
* Armoured Corps  
* Artillery  
* Army Aviation  
* Engineers  
* Signals  
* Air Defence

### **Supporting Services**

* ASC (Army Service Corps)  
* AOC (Army Ordnance Corps)  
* EME (Electrical & Mechanical Engineers)  
* AMC (Army Medical Corps)

# **Army Commands**

The Indian Army has **7 operational commands \+ 1 training command**.

| Command | HQ |
| ----- | ----- |
| Northern Command | Udhampur |
| Western Command | Chandimandir |
| Eastern Command | Kolkata |
| Southern Command | Pune |
| South Western Command | Jaipur |
| Central Command | Lucknow |
| Army Training Command (ARTRAC) | Shimla |
| Central/Strategic Support Elements | Various |

### **Most Sensitive Commands**

* Northern Command → China & Pakistan front  
* Eastern Command → China & Northeast  
* Western Command → Pakistan front

**NEWS**

## **1\. Operation Sindoor & Military Modernisation**

India is continuing to analyse and upgrade its military doctrine after Operation Sindoor.

Major developments:

* Focus on drone warfare  
* Integrated Army-Air Force operations  
* Faster mobilisation and surveillance systems  
* Expansion of indigenous defence technology

This operation is now seen as a major turning point in India’s modern warfare doctrine. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/defence/news/how-the-experience-of-operation-sindoor-is-reshaping-the-indian-armed-forces/articleshow/130959522.cms?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## **2\. Indian Army Expanding Drone & Counter-Drone Capability**

The Indian Army has accelerated induction of:

* Drone units (“Ashni Platoons”)  
* Loitering munitions  
* AI-based surveillance systems  
* Counter-drone grids

The Army is deploying these across infantry formations after lessons from modern conflicts and border threats. ([Defence News India](https://defence.in/threads/a-year-after-operation-sindoor-the-indian-army-successfully-deploys-ashni-platoons-across-all-infantry-formations.17665/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## **3\. Indigenous Weapons & Rocket System Trials**

India recently tested indigenous long-range systems:

* **Suryastra rockets** (150 km & 300 km range)  
* **Vayu Astra-1** loitering munition

These systems are intended to strengthen long-range precision strike capability and battlefield dominance. The Indian Army is also moving toward procurement of these systems. ([The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/defence/news/pune-co-successfully-tests-300km-range-suryastra-rockets-off-odisha-army-procuring-its-launcher-systems/articleshow/131225560.cms?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

### **Bonus Point for SSB Discussion**

You can also mention:

* Replacement of old Cheetah helicopters with indigenous LUH helicopters after a recent Ladakh crash investigation. ([The Economic Times](https://m.economictimes.com/news/defence/cheetah-helicopter-crash-in-ladakh-what-is-the-army-chopper-its-specs-safety-record-and-luh-replacement-plan/articleshow/131281456.cms?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
* India’s increasing focus on AI warfare, cyber warfare, and drone combat. ([The Economic Times](https://m.economictimes.com/news/defence/artificial-intelligence-is-rapidly-transforming-modern-warfare-enabling-real-time-intelligence-autonomous-drones-and-faster-battlefield-decision-making-across-global-conflicts-/articleshow/130545354.cms?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**IEEE**

# **1\. What is IEEE? What is its full form?**

### **Answer**

> IEEE stands for Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. It is one of the world’s largest professional technical organizations. It publishes high-quality research papers, technical standards, and promotes innovation in engineering, electronics, AI, robotics, communication, and computer science.

### **Extra Point**

You can add:

> “Many important technology standards like Wi-Fi standards are associated with IEEE.”

---

# **2\. Why did you choose this research topic?**

### **Answer**

> I was interested in computer vision and autonomous navigation systems. I wanted to work on a practical problem where a camera can help in navigation and collision avoidance. Such systems are useful in robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, and assistive technologies.

### **SSB Impression**

Shows:

* practical thinking  
* innovation mindset  
* problem-solving ability

---

# **3\. Explain your project in simple words.**

### **Answer**

> My research paper focuses on using cameras to detect obstacles and help in navigation. The system processes visual input from the camera, identifies nearby objects or obstacles, estimates their position or movement, and helps avoid collision. The goal is to improve safe navigation using computer vision techniques.

### **Very Important Tip**

DO NOT overcomplicate.  
SSB officers like:

* clarity  
* confidence  
* simplicity

---

# **4\. What technologies or concepts did you use?**

### **Answer**

> The project mainly involved computer vision concepts such as image processing, object detection, depth estimation, and navigation logic. I also worked with programming tools and algorithms related to camera-based perception systems.

If they ask deeper:  
You can mention:

* OpenCV  
* Depth estimation  
* Stereo vision  
* Object detection  
* AI/ML models (if used)

---

# **5\. How can your project help the Army?**

### **BEST QUESTION FOR SSB**

### **Answer**

> Such systems can help in autonomous military vehicles, surveillance robots, drone navigation, and collision avoidance in difficult terrains. Camera-based systems can improve situational awareness and reduce human risk during dangerous operations.

### **Strong Finish**

> “Modern warfare is increasingly moving toward AI, robotics, and autonomous systems, so such technologies have future military relevance.”

---

# **Bonus Questions They May Ask**

## **“What was your role in the paper?”**

Answer honestly:

* algorithm development  
* coding  
* testing  
* documentation  
* experimentation

---

## **“What challenges did you face?”**

Good answer:

> “Accurate obstacle detection in varying lighting conditions and improving navigation reliability were challenging parts.”

---

## **“What did you learn from research work?”**

Excellent answer:

> “Research taught me patience, analytical thinking, teamwork, and how to solve problems systematically.”

---

# **VERY IMPORTANT SSB TIP**

When speaking about your paper:

* avoid memorized textbook language  
* speak naturally  
* explain as if explaining to a non-technical person

That creates the impression of:

* confidence  
* clarity of thought  
* leadership communication

which are important Officer Like Qualities (OLQs).
